## Motivation

Qwen3.5-397B-A17B (NVFP4) low-latency decode on GB300, TP8, MTP (top-k 1, 7 draft tokens). With the NVIDIA megakernel plugin, the GPU part of a decode round gets short enough that SGLang's host work becomes the bottleneck: input staging between graphs, the verify's eager sampling and commits, and the scheduler's per-pass TP syncs. This PR moves that work into CUDA graphs, into fewer launches, or off the critical path. It is the Qwen3.5 counterpart of sgl-project/sglang#45450.

This PR contains no megakernel code. It is independent of the wiring PR, sgl-project/sglang#45266: both are based on main, and either can merge first. The plugin is sgl-project/sgl-nvidia-mega#20.

Every new code path is behind an environment switch that defaults to off. With all switches off, the same GPU operations run in the same order as on main; the accuracy tests below check this. Note that main's Qwen3.5 AgentX recipes (`docs/src/snippets/agentx/Qwen/qwen3.5.jsx`) already set six of these switches to `1`.

## Modifications

One commit per change. The TPS/User figures are what removing that change alone would cost on the full stack (this PR + #45266 + plugin, TP8, one request, 128K) ¹.

1. **Post-verify CUDA graphs** (`SGLANG_ENABLE_EAGLE_POST_VERIFY_CUDA_GRAPH`, ≈ 78 TPS/User): the EAGLE verify's sampling, acceptance and commit outputs replay as CUDA graphs, and the mamba state commit runs on a side stream. Batches a graph cannot reproduce (grammar, penalties, per-request seeds, ...) keep the eager path.
2. **Test:** the post-verify graphs match eager sampling bitwise at batch sizes up to 64.
3. **GDN extend kernels and tables for captured prefill buckets** (no switch; used by 4).
4. **GDN extend in breakable prefill graphs** (`SGLANG_ENABLE_GDN_PREFILL_GRAPH_EXTEND`): prefill no longer leaves the graph at every GDN layer. It does not affect decode; TTFT drops from 82.9 to 40.6 ms for 256-token prompts at TP4.
5. **`small_field_copy`** (`SGLANG_Q35MF_BK_VEC_COPY`, < 1 TPS/User): a JIT kernel that copies up to 16 small fields in one launch, with a 16-byte vectorized path. Item 6 uses it.
6. **Verify-round input staging** (`SGLANG_Q35MF_MKH_N3B`, `_N3C`, ≈ 19 TPS/User):
   - reuse the previous round's mamba track indices;
   - skip input copies that a pre-planned replay already made;
   - load the post-verify graphs' inputs in one launch.
7. **Chain-tree verify build and compact top-k sampling** (`SGLANG_Q35MF_EDGE_CHAIN_TREE`, `_SPARSE_VERIFY_SAMPLING`, ≈ 70 TPS/User):
   - a top-k 1 draft builds its verify chain without the tree mask, which TRT-LLM MHA does not read;
   - a verify whose requests all use a top-k of 2–128 samples on that support instead of the full vocabulary.
8. **Packed verify broadcast** (`SGLANG_Q35MF_EDGE_PACKED_VERIFY_BCAST`, ≈ 3 TPS/User): a sampled verify result reaches the TP group in one broadcast instead of three.
9. **Scheduler TP syncs through shared memory** (`SGLANG_Q35MF_EDGE_SHM_SYNC`, `_SHM_SYNC_MULTIHOST`, `_MULTIHOST_TCP`, ≈ 121 TPS/User): the request broadcast and the HiCache ready counts go through a shared-memory table instead of gloo. Across hosts, the counts use one exchange between the host leaders.
10. **Doc:** the `environ.py` section comment names SGLang branch `nvidia/qwen35-agentx-gb300`, which reads the same switch names.

¹ Measured on an earlier head of the full stack (1,267 TPS/User at P50). Items 1, 7 and 9 are derived from host-time and Kineto measurements rather than separate runs, so the rows do not add up. Four host-side items of earlier heads were dropped: together they gave ~1.3% for 1,204 production lines.

## Accuracy Tests

GB300, real acceptance, GSM8K on a fixed 250-question subset.

| check | result |
|---|---|
| Every switch off vs main, Qwen3.5 TP8, greedy at concurrency 1 and 16 | 250 / 250 texts identical (main vs main: 250 / 250). Same 46 Triton kernels and 8 JIT modules compiled; same KV cache and memory. |
| Every switch off vs main, gpt-oss-120b + EAGLE3, TP2, HiCache on | texts differing from main: 39 / 39 (main vs main: 64 / 69); this model's greedy output varies across restarts |
| Full stack (this PR + #45266 + plugin) vs the development build | greedy 0.980 vs 0.980 (249 / 250 identical); sampled 0.976 vs 0.984; acceptance length ratio 1.000 / 0.998 |
| Full stack vs #45266 + plugin without this PR | greedy 0.980 vs 0.980 (250 / 250 identical); sampled 0.976 vs 0.988; acceptance length ratio 1.000 / 1.006 |

On CPU, the changed test files and the speculative and megakernel unit tests fail only where main fails on the same machine.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

GB300, TP8 across two 4-GPU trays. Static decode of one request at 128K context with forced acceptance 4.80 (`SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=4.80`), about 1,780 rounds per server start. TPS/User = 4.80 tokens / round time. Rows 1–4 are the mean of two pairs of trays run in opposite orders. The plugin was measured at `3509187d74`, an earlier revision of sgl-project/sgl-nvidia-mega#20; the PR head differs only by an opt-in for more than one request, off by default.

| configuration | TPS/User P50 | TPS/User P90 |
|---|---|---|
| main | 706.4 | 700.3 |
| main + this PR | 752.8 (+6.6%) | 742.5 (+6.0%) |
| main + #45266 + plugin | 765.7 (+8.4%) | 729.6 (+4.2%) |
| main + this PR + #45266 + plugin | 1291.7 (+82.8%) | 1276.0 (+82.2%) |
| the development build (reference) ² | 1275.2 | 1249.5 |

² On a third pair of trays, row 4 reaches 101.0% of the reference at P50 at 128K, and 100.8% / 100.6% and 101.9% / 101.6% (P50 / P90) at 8K and 32K.

With the plugin fixed (rows 3 and 4), this PR adds +68.7% at P50 and +74.9% at P90.

These results were measured on main `28448a86d4`. The branch has since been rebased onto main `b57b5e2286`, where two commits differ only by an import path that sgl-project/sglang#45112 moved; the GPU checks are being repeated on the new base. Without the plugin it adds less, because main's longer GPU step hides much of the host work it removes.

On InferenceX AgentX (TP8, concurrency 11, 3,600 s, one request per server at a time), the full stack scores X 1234.57 against the development build's 1219.51 on the same trays. TPS/User is 1314.35 / 1236.99 against 1302.52 / 1230.18 (P50 / P90).

[by Claude Code] **Severity: perf | Confidence: Medium**

**Issue**

`_wait_rows` spins on `os.sched_yield()` until every peer has published. With `--sleep-on-idle`, only attn-TP rank 0 sleeps (`Scheduler.init_idle_sleeper`, up to 1 s in `poller.poll`). Every other TP rank then spins at 100% CPU for that whole wait in the request-broadcast exchange. On main those ranks block in the gloo broadcast and use no CPU.

**Fix**

Spin for a short, bounded time, then back off with `time.sleep` in growing steps. Or keep the gloo path when `sleep_on_idle` is set.

+"""Shared-memory all-gather of a few small integers among the ranks of one host.
+
+The scheduler loop runs two tiny CPU collectives on every pass (the request
+broadcast size and the HiCache ready counts). Over the gloo backend each one
+costs a few hundred microseconds even when every rank is ready. When all ranks
+of the group share a host, this exchange replaces them with a shared-memory
+table.

+Every stored element carries the call's sequence tag in its high bits, and
+readers check each element on its own. So the protocol needs no ordering
+between stores of different elements, only single-copy atomic aligned 64-bit
+loads and stores. The table is double-buffered by sequence parity: a rank can
+reuse a slot only after every rank has published the next call, which a rank
+does only after it has finished reading the previous call.
+
+Enabled by SGLANG_Q35MF_EDGE_SHM_SYNC=1 (default off). Groups that span hosts
+keep the stock gloo path unless SGLANG_Q35MF_EDGE_SHM_SYNC_MULTIHOST=1 is also

[by Claude Code] **Severity: perf | Confidence: Medium**

**Issue**

GDN sizes its static tables by the whole request pool, while KDA caps them at `SGLANG_KDA_PREFILL_GRAPH_MAX_SEQS=128`. So `max_chunks = cdiv(bucket, 64) + min(bucket, pool_size)`. `chunk_fwd_kernel_o` runs one program per row with no early return: each padded row still loads a full `h` block (only the store is masked). `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h` also allocates `h` for every row in each GDN layer.

**Example**

With a 1024-slot pool and a 2048-token bucket, `max_chunks` is 32 + 1024 = 1056. One 2048-token request has 32 real chunks, so the o-kernel does about 33 times the needed work on every replay.

**Fix**

Cap `prefill_graph_max_seqs` with an env var as KDA does, or return early in `chunk_fwd_kernel_o` for padded rows.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: style | Confidence: High**

**Issue**

The three switches are read with `os.environ.get(...) == "1"` instead of through `Envs` in `environ.py`, which the env-var conventions (`.claude/skills/env-var-conventions`) require. As a result, `SGLANG_Q35MF_EDGE_SHM_SYNC=true` is silently ignored, tests cannot use `envs.X.override`, and the value is read again on every scheduler pass through `get_shm_exchange` and `_shm_count_exchange`.

+"""GDN extend captured inside breakable prefill CUDA graphs.
+
+Without this module a breakable prefill CUDA graph (BCG) breaks at every GDN
+layer and runs the extend chain eagerly: about ten Triton launches plus small
+torch ops, roughly a millisecond of host time per layer. The eager chain derives
+its launch grids and index tables from host-side sequence lengths
+(``prepare_chunk_indices``, ``causal_conv1d_fn``'s ``seq_lens_cpu``, the
+prefix-cache track plan); here they come from static per-bucket tables instead,
+as in kda_prefill_graph.py:
+
+* ``max_seqs`` sequences (``min(bucket, cap)``; batches with more sequences run
+  eagerly, through the runner's replay vote on
+  ``AttentionBackend.prefill_cuda_graph_max_batch_size``),
+* ``max_chunks = cdiv(bucket, 64) + max_seqs`` delta-rule chunks,
+* ``max_conv_blocks = cdiv(bucket, BLOCK_M) + max_seqs`` conv blocks.

detail.body:
## Motivation

Qwen3.5-397B-A17B (NVFP4) low-latency decode on GB300, TP8, MTP (top-k 1, 7 draft tokens). With the NVIDIA megakernel plugin, the GPU part of a decode round gets short enough that SGLang's host work becomes the bottleneck: input staging between graphs, the verify's eager sampling and commits, and the scheduler's per-pass TP syncs. This PR moves that work into CUDA graphs, into fewer launches, or off the critical path. It is the Qwen3.5 counterpart of sgl-project/sglang#45450.

This PR contains no megakernel code. It is independent of the wiring PR, sgl-project/sglang#45266: both are based on main, and either can merge first. The plugin is sgl-project/sgl-nvidia-mega#20.

Every new code path is behind an environment switch that defaults to off. With all switches off, the same GPU operations run in the same order as on main; the accuracy tests below check this. Note that main's Qwen3.5 AgentX recipes (`docs/src/snippets/agentx/Qwen/qwen3.5.jsx`) already set six of these switches to `1`.

## Modifications

One commit per change. The TPS/User figures are what removing that change alone would cost on the full stack (this PR + #45266 + plugin, TP8, one request, 128K) ¹.

1. **Post-verify CUDA graphs** (`SGLANG_ENABLE_EAGLE_POST_VERIFY_CUDA_GRAPH`, ≈ 78 TPS/User): the EAGLE verify's sampling, acceptance and commit outputs replay as CUDA graphs, and the mamba state commit runs on a side stream. Batches a graph cannot reproduce (grammar, penalties, per-request seeds, ...) keep the eager path.
2. **Test:** the post-verify graphs match eager sampling bitwise at batch sizes up to 64.
3. **GDN extend kernels and tables for captured prefill buckets** (no switch; used by 4).
4. **GDN extend in breakable prefill graphs** (`SGLANG_ENABLE_GDN_PREFILL_GRAPH_EXTEND`): prefill no longer leaves the graph at every GDN layer. It does not affect decode; TTFT drops from 82.9 to 40.6 ms for 256-token prompts at TP4.
5. **`small_field_copy`** (`SGLANG_Q35MF_BK_VEC_COPY`, < 1 TPS/User): a JIT kernel that copies up to 16 small fields in one launch, with a 16-byte vectorized path. Item 6 uses it.
6. **Verify-round input staging** (`SGLANG_Q35MF_MKH_N3B`, `_N3C`, ≈ 19 TPS/User):
   - reuse the previous round's mamba track indices;
   - skip input copies that a pre-planned replay already made;
   - load the post-verify graphs' inputs in one launch.
7. **Chain-tree verify build and compact top-k sampling** (`SGLANG_Q35MF_EDGE_CHAIN_TREE`, `_SPARSE_VERIFY_SAMPLING`, ≈ 70 TPS/User):
   - a top-k 1 draft builds its verify chain without the tree mask, which TRT-LLM MHA does not read;
   - a verify whose requests all use a top-k of 2–128 samples on that support instead of the full vocabulary.
8. **Packed verify broadcast** (`SGLANG_Q35MF_EDGE_PACKED_VERIFY_BCAST`, ≈ 3 TPS/User): a sampled verify result reaches the TP group in one broadcast instead of three.
9. **Scheduler TP syncs through shared memory** (`SGLANG_Q35MF_EDGE_SHM_SYNC`, `_SHM_SYNC_MULTIHOST`, `_MULTIHOST_TCP`, ≈ 121 TPS/User): the request broadcast and the HiCache ready counts go through a shared-memory table instead of gloo. Across hosts, the counts use one exchange between the host leaders.
10. **Doc:** the `environ.py` section comment names SGLang branch `nvidia/qwen35-agentx-gb300`, which reads the same switch names.

¹ Measured on an earlier head of the full stack (1,267 TPS/User at P50). Items 1, 7 and 9 are derived from host-time and Kineto measurements rather than separate runs, so the rows do not add up. Four host-side items of earlier heads were dropped: together they gave ~1.3% for 1,204 production lines.

## Accuracy Tests

GB300, real acceptance, GSM8K on a fixed 250-question subset.

| check | result |
|---|---|
| Every switch off vs main, Qwen3.5 TP8, greedy at concurrency 1 and 16 | 250 / 250 texts identical (main vs main: 250 / 250). Same 46 Triton kernels and 8 JIT modules compiled; same KV cache and memory. |
| Every switch off vs main, gpt-oss-120b + EAGLE3, TP2, HiCache on | texts differing from main: 39 / 39 (main vs main: 64 / 69); this model's greedy output varies across restarts |
| Full stack (this PR + #45266 + plugin) vs the development build | greedy 0.980 vs 0.980 (249 / 250 identical); sampled 0.976 vs 0.984; acceptance length ratio 1.000 / 0.998 |
| Full stack vs #45266 + plugin without this PR | greedy 0.980 vs 0.980 (250 / 250 identical); sampled 0.976 vs 0.988; acceptance length ratio 1.000 / 1.006 |

On CPU, the changed test files and the speculative and megakernel unit tests fail only where main fails on the same machine.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

GB300, TP8 across two 4-GPU trays. Static decode of one request at 128K context with forced acceptance 4.80 (`SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=4.80`), about 1,780 rounds per server start. TPS/User = 4.80 tokens / round time. Rows 1–4 are the mean of two pairs of trays run in opposite orders. The plugin was measured at `3509187d74`, an earlier revision of sgl-project/sgl-nvidia-mega#20; the PR head differs only by an opt-in for more than one request, off by default.

| configuration | TPS/User P50 | TPS/User P90 |
|---|---|---|
| main | 706.4 | 700.3 |
| main + this PR | 752.8 (+6.6%) | 742.5 (+6.0%) |
| main + #45266 + plugin | 765.7 (+8.4%) | 729.6 (+4.2%) |
| main + this PR + #45266 + plugin | 1291.7 (+82.8%) | 1276.0 (+82.2%) |
| the development build (reference) ² | 1275.2 | 1249.5 |

² On a third pair of trays, row 4 reaches 101.0% of the reference at P50 at 128K, and 100.8% / 100.6% and 101.9% / 101.6% (P50 / P90) at 8K and 32K.

With the plugin fixed (rows 3 and 4), this PR adds +68.7% at P50 and +74.9% at P90.

These results were measured on main `28448a86d4`. The branch has since been rebased onto main `b57b5e2286`, where two commits differ only by an import path that sgl-project/sglang#45112 moved; the GPU checks are being repeated on the new base. Without the plugin it adds less, because main's longer GPU step hides much of the host work it removes.

On InferenceX AgentX (TP8, concurrency 11, 3,600 s, one request per server at a time), the full stack scores X 1234.57 against the development build's 1219.51 on the same trays. TPS/User is 1314.35 / 1236.99 against 1302.52 / 1230.18 (P50 / P90).

+"""GDN extend captured inside breakable prefill CUDA graphs.
+
+Without this module a breakable prefill CUDA graph (BCG) breaks at every GDN
+layer and runs the extend chain eagerly: about ten Triton launches plus small
+torch ops, roughly a millisecond of host time per layer. The eager chain derives
+its launch grids and index tables from host-side sequence lengths
+(``prepare_chunk_indices``, ``causal_conv1d_fn``'s ``seq_lens_cpu``, the
+prefix-cache track plan); here they come from static per-bucket tables instead,
+as in kda_prefill_graph.py:
+
+* ``max_seqs`` sequences (``min(bucket, cap)``; batches with more sequences run
+  eagerly, through the runner's replay vote on
+  ``AttentionBackend.prefill_cuda_graph_max_batch_size``),
+* ``max_chunks = cdiv(bucket, 64) + max_seqs`` delta-rule chunks,
+* ``max_conv_blocks = cdiv(bucket, BLOCK_M) + max_seqs`` conv blocks.
+
+Before every replay ``fill`` rebuilds the tables from the batch's CPU lengths
+(one host-to-device copy plus a few device copies, no synchronization). The
+captured kernels are the eager ones over fixed grids; padded rows point past
+their sequence or carry ``PAD_SLOT_ID`` and return, so every real chunk computes
+exactly what the eager break computes.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Optional
+
+import msgspec
+import numpy as np
+import torch
+import triton
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.mamba.causal_conv1d_triton import (
+    CAUSAL_CONV1D_FWD_BLOCK_M,
+    PAD_SLOT_ID,
+)
+from sglang.kernels.ops.mamba.gdn_prefill_track import (
+    TRACK_CHUNK_STATE,
+    TRACK_FINAL_STATE,
+)
+from sglang.srt.layers.attention.linear.kda_prefill_graph import KDAPrefillTrackRows
+
+# Delta-rule chunk size of chunk_gated_delta_rule (fla/chunk.py).
+GDN_CHUNK_SIZE = 64
+
+
+def chunk_o_block_size(num_tokens: int) -> int:
+    """chunk_fwd_o's chunk size for a varlen batch of ``num_tokens`` rows."""
+    return min(GDN_CHUNK_SIZE, max(16, triton.next_power_of_2(num_tokens)))
+
+
+def buckets_keep_chunk_o_block_size(capture_num_tokens: list[int]) -> bool:
+    """Whether every batch replays with the chunk_fwd_o chunk size its eager
+    break uses: the break runs on the real token count, the graph on the bucket."""
+    buckets = sorted(capture_num_tokens)
+    for n in range(1, GDN_CHUNK_SIZE + 1):
+        bucket = next((b for b in buckets if b >= n), None)
+        if bucket is not None and chunk_o_block_size(bucket) != chunk_o_block_size(n):
+            return False
+    return True
+
+
+class GDNPrefillGraphMetadata(msgspec.Struct, frozen=True):
+    """Static per-bucket tables read by the captured GDN extend."""
+
+    num_tokens: int
+    max_seqs: int
+    max_chunks: int
+    max_conv_blocks: int
+    # Allocates and records the prefix-cache snapshot copies.
+    track: bool
+
+    # One int32 device buffer, refreshed by a single copy, and its views.
+    packed: torch.Tensor
+    cu_seqlens: torch.Tensor  # [max_seqs + 1]
+    chunk_indices: torch.Tensor  # [max_chunks, 2] (seq, chunk), sequence-major
+    chunk_offsets: torch.Tensor  # [max_seqs + 1]
+    conv_block_table: torch.Tensor  # [max_conv_blocks, 2] (seq, block)
+    track_mode: torch.Tensor  # [max_seqs]
+    track_h_row: torch.Tensor  # [max_seqs] row of the per-chunk states h
+    track_conv_start: torch.Tensor  # [max_seqs]
+    num_logical_tokens: torch.Tensor  # [1]
+    host: np.ndarray  # int32 staging for `packed`
+
+    # Filled on the device from the batch.
+    cache_indices: torch.Tensor  # [max_seqs], PAD_SLOT_ID past the batch
+    has_initial_state: torch.Tensor  # [max_seqs] bool
+    track_dst: torch.Tensor  # [max_seqs] int64
+
+    @classmethod
+    def allocate(
+        cls,
+        *,
+        num_tokens: int,
+        max_seqs_cap: int,
+        track: bool,
+        cache_index_dtype: torch.dtype,
+        device: torch.device,
+    ) -> GDNPrefillGraphMetadata:
+        max_seqs = max(1, min(num_tokens, max_seqs_cap))
+        max_chunks = triton.cdiv(num_tokens, GDN_CHUNK_SIZE) + max_seqs
+        max_conv_blocks = triton.cdiv(num_tokens, CAUSAL_CONV1D_FWD_BLOCK_M) + max_seqs
+        sizes = [
+            max_seqs + 1,  # cu_seqlens
+            2 * max_chunks,  # chunk_indices
+            max_seqs + 1,  # chunk_offsets
+            2 * max_conv_blocks,  # conv_block_table
+            max_seqs,  # track_mode
+            max_seqs,  # track_h_row
+            max_seqs,  # track_conv_start
+            1,  # num_logical_tokens
+        ]
+        packed = torch.zeros(sum(sizes), dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+        views = torch.split(packed, sizes)
+        return cls(
+            num_tokens=num_tokens,
+            max_seqs=max_seqs,
+            max_chunks=max_chunks,
+            max_conv_blocks=max_conv_blocks,
+            track=track,
+            packed=packed,
+            cu_seqlens=views[0],
+            chunk_indices=views[1].view(max_chunks, 2),
+            chunk_offsets=views[2],
+            conv_block_table=views[3].view(max_conv_blocks, 2),
+            track_mode=views[4],
+            track_h_row=views[5],
+            track_conv_start=views[6],
+            num_logical_tokens=views[7],
+            host=np.zeros(sum(sizes), dtype=np.int32),
+            cache_indices=torch.full(
+                (max_seqs,), PAD_SLOT_ID, dtype=cache_index_dtype, device=device
+            ),
+            has_initial_state=torch.zeros(max_seqs, dtype=torch.bool, device=device),
+            track_dst=torch.zeros(max_seqs, dtype=torch.int64, device=device),
+        )
+
+    def can_fit(self, extend_seq_lens: list[int]) -> bool:
+        return (
+            len(extend_seq_lens) <= self.max_seqs
+            and sum(extend_seq_lens) <= self.num_tokens
+        )
+
+    def fill(
+        self,
+        *,
+        extend_seq_lens: list[int],
+        cache_indices: torch.Tensor,
+        extend_prefix_lens: torch.Tensor,
+        track_rows: Optional[KDAPrefillTrackRows],
+    ) -> None:
+        """Rebuild the tables for this batch. ``cache_indices`` and
+        ``extend_prefix_lens`` are the batch's device tensors."""
+        bs = len(extend_seq_lens)
+        assert self.can_fit(extend_seq_lens), (
+            f"batch of {bs} sequences / {sum(extend_seq_lens)} tokens exceeds the "
+            f"captured bounds ({self.max_seqs} / {self.num_tokens})"
+        )
+        self._write_host_tables(
+            lens=np.asarray(extend_seq_lens, dtype=np.int64), track_rows=track_rows
+        )
+        # A pinned block from the caching host allocator keeps the copy
+        # asynchronous and is not reused before the copy completes.
+        self.packed.copy_(torch.from_numpy(self.host).pin_memory(), non_blocking=True)
+        self.cache_indices[:bs].copy_(cache_indices[:bs])
+        self.cache_indices[bs:].fill_(PAD_SLOT_ID)
+        torch.gt(extend_prefix_lens[:bs], 0, out=self.has_initial_state[:bs])
+        self.has_initial_state[bs:].fill_(False)
+        if track_rows is not None:
+            self.track_dst[:bs].copy_(track_rows.dst[:bs])
+
+    def _write_host_tables(
+        self, *, lens: np.ndarray, track_rows: Optional[KDAPrefillTrackRows]
+    ) -> None:
+        """Write every host-built table into ``self.host`` in ``packed`` order."""
+        bs = lens.shape[0]
+        total = int(lens.sum())
+
+        # Padded sequences are empty and sit at the end.
+        cu = np.empty(self.max_seqs + 1, dtype=np.int64)
+        cu[0] = 0
+        np.cumsum(lens, out=cu[1 : bs + 1])
+        cu[bs + 1 :] = total
+        o = self._write(o=0, values=cu)
+
+        # Sequence-major (seq, chunk) rows: chunk_fwd_o reads the per-chunk states
+        # by row, chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h writes them at chunk_offsets[seq] + chunk.
+        # Padded rows name the chunk just past sequence 0, which every chunk
+        # kernel masks or returns on.
+        n_chunks = (lens + GDN_CHUNK_SIZE - 1) // GDN_CHUNK_SIZE
+        o = self._write_pairs(
+            o=o, counts=n_chunks, rows=self.max_chunks, pad=(0, int(n_chunks[0]))
+        )
+        offsets = np.empty(self.max_seqs + 1, dtype=np.int64)
+        offsets[0] = 0
+        np.cumsum(n_chunks, out=offsets[1 : bs + 1])
+        offsets[bs + 1 :] = offsets[bs]
+        o = self._write(o=o, values=offsets)
+
+        n_blocks = (lens + CAUSAL_CONV1D_FWD_BLOCK_M - 1) // CAUSAL_CONV1D_FWD_BLOCK_M
+        o = self._write_pairs(
+            o=o, counts=n_blocks, rows=self.max_conv_blocks, pad=(PAD_SLOT_ID, 0)
+        )
+
+        track_mode = np.zeros(self.max_seqs, dtype=np.int64)
+        track_h_row = np.zeros(self.max_seqs, dtype=np.int64)
+        track_conv_start = np.zeros(self.max_seqs, dtype=np.int64)
+        if track_rows is not None:
+            # Same source rows as the eager plan: h_offsets[row] + chunk.
+            for row, chunk in track_rows.chunk_rows:
+                track_h_row[row] = offsets[row] + chunk
+                track_mode[row] = TRACK_CHUNK_STATE
+            for row in track_rows.final_rows:
+                track_mode[row] = TRACK_FINAL_STATE
+            for row, aligned_len in track_rows.conv_rows:
+                track_conv_start[row] = cu[row] + aligned_len - track_rows.conv_len
+        o = self._write(o=o, values=track_mode)
+        o = self._write(o=o, values=track_h_row)
+        o = self._write(o=o, values=track_conv_start)
+        o = self._write(o=o, values=np.array([total]))
+        assert o == self.host.shape[0]
+
+    def _write(self, *, o: int, values: np.ndarray) -> int:
+        self.host[o : o + values.shape[0]] = values
+        return o + values.shape[0]
+
+    def _write_pairs(
+        self, *, o: int, counts: np.ndarray, rows: int, pad: tuple[int, int]
+    ) -> int:
+        """Write (seq, index) rows, `counts[seq]` indices per sequence, into a
+        [rows, 2] table at `o`, padding the tail with `pad`."""
+        n = int(counts.sum())
+        table = self.host[o : o + 2 * rows].reshape(rows, 2)
+        if n:
+            table[:n, 0] = np.repeat(np.arange(counts.shape[0]), counts)
+            table[:n, 1] = np.arange(n) - np.repeat(np.cumsum(counts) - counts, counts)
+        table[n:, 0] = pad[0]
+        table[n:, 1] = pad[1]
+        return o + 2 * rows

+"""Shared-memory all-gather of a few small integers among the ranks of one host.
+
+The scheduler loop runs two tiny CPU collectives on every pass (the request
+broadcast size and the HiCache ready counts). Over the gloo backend each one
+costs a few hundred microseconds even when every rank is ready. When all ranks
+of the group share a host, this exchange replaces them with a shared-memory
+table.
+
+Every stored element carries the call's sequence tag in its high bits, and
+readers check each element on its own. So the protocol needs no ordering
+between stores of different elements, only single-copy atomic aligned 64-bit
+loads and stores. The table is double-buffered by sequence parity: a rank can
+reuse a slot only after every rank has published the next call, which a rank
+does only after it has finished reading the previous call.
+
+Enabled by SGLANG_Q35MF_EDGE_SHM_SYNC=1 (default off). Groups that span hosts
+keep the stock gloo path unless SGLANG_Q35MF_EDGE_SHM_SYNC_MULTIHOST=1 is also
+set: then each host exchanges through shared memory and only the host leaders
+meet in one small gloo all_gather (HierTagExchange).
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import ctypes
+import logging
+import os
+import socket
+import time
+from array import array
+from multiprocessing import shared_memory
+from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Sequence
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import torch
+import torch.distributed as dist
+
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_device
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+_TAG_BITS = 23
+_VAL_BITS = 40
+_TAG_MASK = (1 << _TAG_BITS) - 1
+_VAL_MASK = (1 << _VAL_BITS) - 1
+
+
+class ShmTagExchange:
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        group: dist.ProcessGroup,
+        kind: str,
+        width: int = 8,
+        rows: Optional[int] = None,
+    ):
+        from sglang.srt.utils.stale_shm_cleanup import make_shm_name
+
+        self.group = group
+        self.world = dist.get_world_size(group)
+        self.rank = dist.get_rank(group)
+        self.width = width
+        # One row per rank for allgather; publish_rows / read_rows may use any row count.
+        self.rows = self.world if rows is None else rows
+        self.seq = 0
+        self.timeout_s = float(

+            self.shm = shared_memory.SharedMemory(
+                create=True, size=nbytes, name=make_shm_name(f"edgex{kind}")
+            )
+            self.shm.buf[:nbytes] = bytes(nbytes)

+        else:
+            recv = [None]
+            dist.broadcast_object_list(recv, src=ranks[0], group=group)

+            with patch(

+            ):

+            self.shm.buf
+        )
+        dist.barrier(group=group)
+
+    def allgather(self, values: Sequence[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
+        """Every rank passes the same number of values, each in [0, 2**40)."""
+        n = len(values)
+        assert n <= self.width and self.rows == self.world
+        self.seq += 1
+        tag = self.seq & _TAG_MASK
+        base = (self.seq & 1) * self.rows * self.width
+        self._store(base + self.rank * self.width, values, tag)
+        return self._wait_rows(base, n, tag)
+
+    def publish_rows(self, table: Sequence[Sequence[int]]) -> None:
+        """Single writer: stores every row of this call; the other ranks call read_rows."""
+        self.seq += 1
+        tag = self.seq & _TAG_MASK
+        base = (self.seq & 1) * self.rows * self.width
+        for r, row in enumerate(table):
+            self._store(base + r * self.width, row, tag)
+
+    def read_rows(self, n: int) -> List[List[int]]:
+        self.seq += 1
+        tag = self.seq & _TAG_MASK
+        return self._wait_rows((self.seq & 1) * self.rows * self.width, n, tag)
+
+    def _store(self, start: int, values: Sequence[int], tag: int) -> None:
+        tagged = tag << _VAL_BITS
+        for i, v in enumerate(values):
+            if not 0 <= v <= _VAL_MASK:
+                raise ValueError(f"shm exchange value out of range: {v}")
+            self.table[start + i] = tagged | v
+
+    def _wait_rows(self, base: int, n: int, tag: int) -> List[List[int]]:
+        t = self.table
+        out: List[List[int]] = []
+        deadline = None
+        for r in range(self.rows):
+            row = base + r * self.width
+            vals = []
+            for i in range(n):
+                x = t[row + i]
+                while (x >> _VAL_BITS) != tag:
+                    if deadline is None:
+                        deadline = time.monotonic() + self.timeout_s
+                    elif time.monotonic() > deadline:
+                        raise RuntimeError(
+                            f"shm exchange timed out after {self.timeout_s:.0f}s waiting "
+                            f"for rank {r} (seq {self.seq}); a peer scheduler is stuck or dead"
+                        )
+                    os.sched_yield()
+                    x = t[row + i]
+                vals.append(x & _VAL_MASK)
+            out.append(vals)
+        return out
+
+    def close(self):
+        try:
+            del self.table
+            self.shm.close()
+            if self._creator:
+                self.shm.unlink()
+        except Exception:
+            pass

+class _LeaderLink:
+    """Persistent TCP connection between the two host leaders; one send and one exact
+    receive per call (payloads are a few hundred bytes, so the sends never block)."""
+
+    def __init__(self, leaders: dist.ProcessGroup, first: bool, timeout_s: float):
+        from sglang.srt.utils.network import get_local_ip_auto
+
+        server = None
+        box: List[Optional[tuple]] = [None]
+        if first:
+            server = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
+            server.bind(("0.0.0.0", 0))
+            server.listen(1)
+            box[0] = (get_local_ip_auto(), server.getsockname()[1])
+        src = dist.get_process_group_ranks(leaders)[0]
+        dist.broadcast_object_list(box, src=src, group=leaders)
+        if first:
+            server.settimeout(timeout_s)
+            self.sock, _ = server.accept()
+            server.close()
+        else:
+            self.sock = socket.create_connection(box[0], timeout=timeout_s)
+        self.sock.settimeout(timeout_s)
+        self.sock.setsockopt(socket.IPPROTO_TCP, socket.TCP_NODELAY, 1)
+
+    def swap(self, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
+        self.sock.sendall(len(payload).to_bytes(4, "little") + payload)
+        size = int.from_bytes(self._recv_exact(4), "little")
+        return self._recv_exact(size)
+
+    def _recv_exact(self, n: int) -> bytes:
+        buf = bytearray()
+        while len(buf) < n:
+            chunk = self.sock.recv(n - len(buf))
+            if not chunk:
+                raise RuntimeError("EDGE leader link closed by the peer leader")
+            buf += chunk
+        return bytes(buf)
+

+class HierTagExchange:
+    """ShmTagExchange.allgather for a group that spans hosts: ranks exchange through
+    shared memory on their host, and only the host leaders run one gloo all_gather."""
+
+    def __init__(self, group: dist.ProcessGroup, kind: str, width: int = 8):
+        ranks = dist.get_process_group_ranks(group)
+        me = dist.get_rank(group)
+        hostnames: List[Optional[str]] = [None] * len(ranks)
+        dist.all_gather_object(hostnames, socket.gethostname(), group=group)
+        hosts = list(dict.fromkeys(hostnames))
+        # Group ranks per host, in group-rank order (new_group keeps that order).
+        self.members = [
+            [i for i, h in enumerate(hostnames) if h == host] for host in hosts
+        ]
+        # new_group is collective over the default group: every rank creates every subgroup.
+        local_groups = [
+            dist.new_group([ranks[i] for i in m], backend="gloo") for m in self.members
+        ]
+        self.leaders = dist.new_group(
+            [ranks[m[0]] for m in self.members], backend="gloo"
+        )
+        host = hosts.index(hostnames[me])
+        self.is_leader = me == self.members[host][0]
+        self.host = host
+        self.world = len(ranks)
+        self.width = width
+        self.local_max = max(len(m) for m in self.members)
+        self.local = ShmTagExchange(local_groups[host], kind + "l", width)
+        self.full = ShmTagExchange(
+            local_groups[host], kind + "f", width, rows=self.world
+        )
+        # Two hosts: the leaders swap rows over one TCP connection instead of a gloo all_gather.
+        self.link = None
+        if (
+            self.is_leader
+            and len(self.members) == 2
+            and envs.SGLANG_Q35MF_EDGE_MULTIHOST_TCP.get()
+        ):
+            self.link = _LeaderLink(self.leaders, host == 0, self.local.timeout_s)
+
+    def allgather(self, values: Sequence[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
+        n = len(values)
+        rows_here = self.local.allgather(values)
+        if not self.is_leader:
+            return self.full.read_rows(n)
+        mine = [v for row in rows_here for v in row]
+        if self.link is not None:
+            peer = array("q")
+            peer.frombytes(self.link.swap(array("q", mine).tobytes()))
+            per_host = (
+                [mine, peer.tolist()] if self.host == 0 else [peer.tolist(), mine]
+            )
+        else:
+            flat = torch.zeros(self.local_max * n, dtype=torch.int64)
+            flat[: len(mine)] = torch.tensor(mine, dtype=torch.int64)
+            outs = [torch.empty_like(flat) for _ in self.members]
+            dist.all_gather(outs, flat, group=self.leaders)
+            per_host = [out.tolist() for out in outs]
+        table: List[List[int]] = [[] for _ in range(self.world)]
+        for m, vals in zip(self.members, per_host):
+            for j, g in enumerate(m):
+                table[g] = vals[j * n : (j + 1) * n]
+        self.full.publish_rows(table)
+        return table
+

+def get_shm_exchange(
+    group: Optional[dist.ProcessGroup], kind: str, multihost: bool = False
+):
+    """Collective on first call per (group, kind): every rank of the group must call it
+    at the same point. Returns None (stock path) when disabled, under --sleep-on-idle,
+    or when the group spans hosts and the caller did not opt in with multihost=True."""
+    if group is None:
+        return None
+    key = (id(group), kind)
+    if key not in _EXCHANGES:
+        if (
+            not envs.SGLANG_Q35MF_EDGE_SHM_SYNC.get()
+            # an idle rank 0 sleeps in its poller; the waiting ranks would spin meanwhile
+            or get_device().sleep_on_idle
+            or dist.get_world_size(group) <= 1
+        ):
+            _EXCHANGES[key] = None
+        else:
+            from sglang.srt.distributed.parallel_state import in_the_same_node_as
+
+            same = in_the_same_node_as(group, source_rank=0)
+            if all(same):
+                _EXCHANGES[key] = ShmTagExchange(group, kind)
+                logger.info(
+                    "EDGE shm exchange '%s' enabled for a %d-rank group",
+                    kind,
+                    dist.get_world_size(group),
+                )
+            elif (
+                multihost
+                and envs.SGLANG_Q35MF_EDGE_SHM_SYNC_MULTIHOST.get()
+                and dist.get_world_size() == dist.get_world_size(group)
+            ):
+                # Only when this group is the whole default group, so the subgroup
+                # creation inside is collective over exactly these ranks.
+                _EXCHANGES[key] = HierTagExchange(group, kind)
+                logger.info(
+                    "EDGE hierarchical exchange '%s' enabled for a %d-rank group on %d hosts",
+                    kind,
+                    dist.get_world_size(group),
+                    len(_EXCHANGES[key].members),
+                )
+            else:
+                _EXCHANGES[key] = None
+    return _EXCHANGES[key]
+

+outputs and, on a side stream, the mamba state commit, for every batch a graph can

+import logging

+    """The forced acceptance lengths' generator (SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN), seeded
+    alike on every rank from the server seed."""
+    return torch.Generator().manual_seed(

+    size, sampling mode, forced acceptance, tracking and the verify logits buffer."""

+        self._target_worker = target_worker
+        self._graphs = _PostVerifyGraphs(
+            body=self._body,
+            commit=self._commit,

+    def run(
+        self,

+        max_top_k: Optional[int] = None,

+eager GDNAttnBackend.forward_extend.

+One bucket is captured once, then replayed for batches of different shapes:
+several sequences, cached prefixes, padding past the batch, chunk-aligned and
+unaligned prefix-cache snapshots, and a batch without tracking. Each replay must
+match the eager path bit for bit on the output, the conv / SSM state pools and
+the track slots, for FP32 and BF16 SSM states.
+"""

+    GDNPrefillGraphMetadata,
+)

+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase

+

+DIM = (2 * HEADS + V_HEADS) * HEAD_DIM
+BUCKET, MAX_SEQS = 512, 16
+NUM_SLOTS = 48
+CHUNK = 64
+
+
+def _layer():
+    g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(7)
+
+    def randn(*shape, dtype=torch.bfloat16, scale=0.2):
+        return (torch.randn(*shape, generator=g, device="cuda") * scale).to(dtype)
+
+    return SimpleNamespace(
+        layer_id=0,
+        num_q_heads=HEADS,
+        num_k_heads=HEADS,
+        num_v_heads=V_HEADS,
+        head_q_dim=HEAD_DIM,
+        head_k_dim=HEAD_DIM,
+        head_v_dim=HEAD_DIM,
+        q_dim=HEADS * HEAD_DIM,
+        k_dim=HEADS * HEAD_DIM,
+        v_dim=V_HEADS * HEAD_DIM,

+def _backend(conv_pool, ssm_pool):
+    """The production backend on test pools: slot of request i is i + 1."""
+    backend = GDNAttnBackend.__new__(GDNAttnBackend)
+    cache = SimpleNamespace(conv=[conv_pool], temporal=ssm_pool)
+    backend.req_to_token_pool = SimpleNamespace(
+        mamba2_layer_cache=lambda layer_id: cache,
+        get_mamba_indices=lambda req_pool_indices: (req_pool_indices + 1).to(

+        translate_mamba_indices=lambda indices: indices,
+    )

+    backend.accept_lens_pool = None
+    backend.prefill_graph_metadata = None
+    backend.kernel_dispatcher = GDNKernelDispatcher(
+        LinearAttnKernelBackend.TRITON,
+        LinearAttnKernelBackend.TRITON,
+        LinearAttnKernelBackend.TRITON,
+    )
+    return backend
+
+
+def _batch(extend_lens, prefix_lens, track=None):
+    """A ForwardBatch stand-in. ``track[row] = tracked length`` (from the
+    prefix) marks prefix-cache snapshot rows; their track slots follow the
+    cache slots (NUM_SLOTS // 2 + row)."""
+    bs = len(extend_lens)
+    dev = "cuda"

+    batch = SimpleNamespace(
+        forward_mode=ForwardMode.EXTEND,

+            ):

+            self.shm.buf

+        dist.barrier(group=group)

+    def allgather(self, values: Sequence[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
+        """Every rank passes the same number of values, each in [0, 2**40)."""
+        n = len(values)
+        assert n <= self.width and self.rows == self.world
+        self.seq += 1
+        tag = self.seq & _TAG_MASK
+        base = (self.seq & 1) * self.rows * self.width

+        return self._wait_rows(base, n, tag)
+
+    def publish_rows(self, table: Sequence[Sequence[int]]) -> None:
+        """Single writer: stores every row of this call; the other ranks call read_rows."""
+        self.seq += 1
+        tag = self.seq & _TAG_MASK
+        base = (self.seq & 1) * self.rows * self.width
+        for r, row in enumerate(table):
+            self._store(base + r * self.width, row, tag)
+
+    def read_rows(self, n: int) -> List[List[int]]:
+        self.seq += 1
+        tag = self.seq & _TAG_MASK

+    def _store(self, start: int, values: Sequence[int], tag: int) -> None:
+        tagged = tag << _VAL_BITS
